key_insight: DemoPSD improves on-policy self-distillation by adaptively blending teacher and student outputs with a reverse-KL barycenter target, reducing privileged-information leakage while preserving exploration.
engineering_relevance: This is relevant for training reasoning LLMs because it offers a safer distillation strategy that can improve cross-domain generalization without collapsing the model into overfit teacher behavior.
method: Compute token-level disagreement between teacher and student distributions.
Use disagreement to adaptively set the blending weight for a reverse-KL barycenter target.
Train the student to match this selective target rather than the full teacher distribution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on SciKnowEval across four scientific fields, where DemoPSD outperforms GRPO and SDPO and also generalizes better to out-of-distribution GPQA benchmarks.
watch_item: The adaptive token-level blending and distribution matching may be sensitive to how disagreement is estimated and tuned during training, which could affect stability and reproducibility.
